gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-001 identifies the same false fixed-R asymptotic claim: mesh refinement alone is said to yield whole-space eigenvalues, although the upper endpoint remains the finite-radius Dirichlet value and the lower endpoint remains the finite-radius Neumann-based corrected bound. It also correctly identifies that R must tend to infinity for convergence to the whole-space eigenvalue.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: Both the gold issue and ISSUE-001 diagnose the incorrect use of the h_max→0 limit as implying convergence of both fixed-R bounds to the whole-space eigenvalue, thereby omitting the persistent finite-R truncation and lower-bound exterior correction.

component_coverage.gold_component: The claim that fixed-domain mesh refinement makes the upper and lower bounds converge to the whole-space eigenvalue is false because finite-R residuals remain: the upper endpoint converges to the finite-radius Dirichlet eigenvalue, while the lower endpoint retains its finite-radius Neumann/exterior correction.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction explicitly holds R fixed, gives the distinct finite-R limits of both endpoints, states that neither equals the whole-space eigenvalue unless R→∞, and proposes the corresponding corrected convergence statement. Thus it recognizes the complete substantive gold concern.
